memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'You shall not make for yourself an image in the form of anything in heaven
above or on the earth beneath or in the waters below. You shall not bow down to
them or worship them.'" - Ex 20:4-5a (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The first command says who to worship. This one says how.

The problem with an image is not artistic. It is that any representation of God
must be smaller than God. Carve Him and you have already reduced Him. Whatever
you make will reflect your own imagination back at you.

This matters more than we think, because we all do it mentally. We form a picture
of God and then relate to that picture. A God who is mostly disappointed in us. A
God who is comfortable with everything we do. A God who mainly wants us
successful. None of these are carved from wood, but they are still images, and
they are still smaller than He is.

The correction is Scripture. We do not get to decide what God is like; He tells
us. The Bible is God's self-portrait, and it consistently includes things we
would not have invented.

Notice one exception God Himself made. He forbade images of Himself, and then
came in person. Paul writes that Christ "is the image of the invisible God"
(Col 1:15). Jesus said, "Anyone who has seen me has seen the Father" (John
14:9).

No image we make will do. The one God gave is a person.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What picture of God do you carry that Scripture might correct?
2. Where did that picture actually come from?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, tear down the false images I have made of You. Show me who You really
are through Your Word and through Jesus. Amen.
